text.p: Marks & Spencer, Britain's biggest clothing retailer, said Tuesday a return of consumer confidence helped boost its first-half profits by 11.6 percent, but the results were below market expectations.

Pretax profits in the half year to Sept. 28 rose to 430.1 million pounds ($704 million) from 385.4 million ($631 million). But the market had expected profits of about 450 million pounds ($737 million).
Sales rose 9 percent to 3.53 billion pounds ($5.8 billion).
Higher costs associated with hiring 2,000 extra staff in Britain hurt profits, industry analysts said.
They said the investment in staff would pay dividends in the long run, but they were disappointed with the smaller than expected profit increase.
The group, which also has stores in North America, continental Europe and Asia, said the additional staff would increase costs, but were essential for customer service.
"Although this will inevitably increase our cost base, it is essential that we invest in appropriate levels of customer service," Chairman Sir Richard Greenbury said.
He said that consumer confidence seemed to be returning in Britain, where sales were up by 8.4 percent to 221 million pounds ($362 million).
"We have increased our market share in clothing, and have held our position in foods. We have maintained our margins across the business," he said.
Brooks Brothers, with stores in Japan as well as the United States, returned to a profit of 1.1 million pounds ($1.8 million) after a loss of 2.5 million ($4.1 million) last time.
Home furnishings benefited from the upturn in the British housing market, with sales up 27 percent. In foods, sales rose 6.6 percent to 1.23 billion pounds ($2 billion).
Overseas sales, including franchises, rose 12 percent to 591 million pounds ($968 million), while profits were up 36 percent to 17 million pounds ($27.8 million).
